questions.q: According to this lesson, how did Chapter 4's field types directly feed into the capstone's Lesson 33 work?
options: They didn't connect to the capstone at all
They let you read Incident's Choice, Reference, and Journal fields with understanding instead of guesswork
They only applied to the Problem table, not Incident
They replaced the need to check the dictionary entirely
questions.explain: Chapter 4's field-type lessons are exactly what let Lesson 33 interpret priority, caller_id, and work_notes correctly rather than guessing.

questions.q: Why did this capstone use a realistic, undocumented instance instead of a guided click-through?
options: Because guided click-throughs are more thorough
Because real screenshots were unavailable
Because the real skill being tested is figuring out an unfamiliar instance with no script, which is the actual job
Because a realistic instance is easier to build than a tutorial
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says a guided tour teaches following a script — not what to do when there isn't one, which is the real admin skill.

questions.q: Which course comes immediately after this one in the ServiceNow Administrator path?
options: Flow Designer Fundamentals
ServiceNow System Administration
ServiceNow Scripting with GlideRecord
Technical Architect Capstone
questions.explain: This course is course 2 of 14; System Administration is course 3, and it assumes this course's navigation and dictionary skills are already solid.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why would a later Flow Designer course expect you to already understand field types like Choice and Journal?
options: It wouldn't — Flow Designer doesn't interact with fields
Because a flow that checks priority or writes to work_notes only makes sense if you already know what kind of field each one is
Because Flow Designer replaces the need for a dictionary entirely
Because field types only matter for reporting, never for automation
questions.explain: Automations that read or write specific fields rely on already understanding what those fields are and how each type behaves.

questions.q: What three things does this lesson suggest you honestly self-assess before starting course 3?
options: Your typing speed, your Wi-Fi connection, and your screen resolution
Finding a table list unaided, naming a dictionary field's type and its implication, and explaining what a related list shows
Whether you prefer Incident or Problem as a table name
How many PDIs you have registered
questions.explain: The lesson names these three specific checks as the honest readiness bar before moving into System Administration.
